target_customer: Manufacturers and distributors that ship freight and shippers working with trucking companies
problem: Freight coordination (quotes, booking, tracking, paperwork, payment) is done manually by brokers and internal logistics teams.
business_model: AI logistics agent (Wilson) offered free to shippers on its network, with a small fee of 2% to 0.5% when using their own carriers

founders.name: Abdul Basharat
prior_employers: Rose Rocket (YC S16), product lead for network and PLG
founders.background_notes: YC page says he began his career training as a military pilot.

founders.name: Josh Lampen
prior_employers: Rose Rocket (YC S16), founding engineer on Platform team
founders.background_notes: YC page says he played water polo for Canada's National Team.

founders.name: Harman Sahota
previous_startups: Westcore Logistics (scaled to $50M+ revenue in four years, per YC page; later acquired by Cartage)
founders.background_notes: Listed as COO in the YC launch post, not in the YC founder section; a Wayfinder profile calls him co-founder.

technical_complexity.rationale: Agents that quote, book, track and pay freight need integrations with carriers, documents and payments plus reliable LLM behavior, standard engineering with hard operational parts. The company later trained its own logistics model per a 2026 feature.

defensibility.rationale: Combined shipping volume across shippers can improve rates, and the load and rate data compounds, but AI brokerage entrants copied the idea quickly.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent acquired or clearly copied it in sources found; several AI freight startups entered the same wedge after 2024.

market_need_then: Freight brokerage runs on low single digit margins and heavy manual coordination, so shippers and carriers pay brokers for work that language models could automate.

identity.logo: A plain letter C mark in directory listings
identity.mascot_or_character: Wilson, the named AI logistics agent
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct value pitch: 'Your free logistics department'

branding.brand_signature: Wilson, the AI agent persona, and the free logistics department tagline

brand_strength.rationale: Cartage is a real freight word that fits the industry and the Wilson persona is memorable, but no press about the brand itself was found.

pivots.to: Autonomous freight coordination and an AI logistics agent for manufacturers and distributors
pivots.why: Not stated; the YC page mentions $150k ARR from earlier software sales and the acquisition of Westcore Logistics.

outcome_analysis: Cartage raised a reported $3.3M round in October 2024 led by YC and Garage Capital among others, then repositioned around Wilson, an AI agent for manufacturers and distributors. A July 2026 feature says it has raised close to $10M since YC and is working on a Series A. That later claim is unverified. The founders have prior Rose Rocket freight software experience, and no shutdown or acquisition was found.
notes: Other aggregators give $2.4M (VCBacked), $2M (StartupIntros), $3.8M total (Caplight) and a $0.54M seed in Mar 2024 (CB Insights); these conflict and are unverified. Round stage recorded as other because FreightWaves calls it an investment round without a stage label (SeedTable calls it seed). The claim of close to $10M raised since YC comes from a single 2026 feature seen only in a search snippet and is not recorded as rounds. No dated competitor sources near mid 2024 were found; Freight Hero, FleetWorks, HappyRobot and others appeared with unconfirmed launch dates.
